_comment: THE SNAPSHOT FORMAT TOKEN, and which tokens this tree can read. Data-Contract.md §5.2.
THIS FILE IS DATA FOR THE SAME REASON `refusal-reasons.json` IS: two languages need it.
`tools/chain/lib/snapshot-format.mjs` is the producer side and
`src/blocktracer/chain/snapshot_format.nim` is the reader side, which reads this file with
`staticRead` at compile time. A version gate that is spelled twice is two gates, and the
cost of that is exactly what this file was created to stop: before it, the literal
`blocktracer/chain-snapshot@1` appeared at ten sites — four producers, two consumers, one
test helper and three committed fixtures — and the reader's gate was a bare `!=` against
its own copy.
ING-3 made `refusalReason` MANDATORY on every untraced row: `auditRefusals` refuses a
snapshot without it, and that gate runs in the write path of every producer. That is a
NEW REQUIRED MEMBER, which Data-Contract.md §3's additive-only rule does not permit
inside one version — and the proof it is not additive is that
`tools/chain/migrate-refusal-reasons.mjs` had to exist, because the committed `@1`
captures could not pass the gate their own producers now run. Left at `@1`, the token
would mean two different things and nothing in the artifact could say which.
It reads it, FULLY, with `refusalReason` optional — which is the behaviour it has always
had. §3's rule is that a version the reader does not support is refused BY NAME rather
than misread, and §5.2 that an unknown token is never partially read. `@1` is neither
unknown nor partially read: `readable` enumerates it, and the only member `@2` adds is one
the reader already treated as optional. What changes is that on `@2` the reader ENFORCES
it, so the token is a checkable statement about the tree rather than decoration.
A tree may therefore be `@1` or `@2` and never both: `mandatoryMembers` is what separates
them, and a producer that emits a mandatory member must emit the token that requires it.
── THE OUTCOME PARTITION, HERE BECAUSE THE GATE NEEDS IT ──────────────────────────────
"Every untraced row carries a reason" is only checkable against a definition of untraced,
and the three populations are not interchangeable:
traced        a container exists and it steps
untraced      this pipeline declined it, and the reason id says which member
chainAbsent   the chain published no such execution — Aztec's private half. These carry
a SENTENCE and NO reason id, because the closed set is a set of things WE
did and this is not one of them (Trace-Artifacts.md §6)
`tools/chain/lib/refusal.mjs` reads these rather than declaring its own copy; the
reasoning behind each is in that file's headers.
